title: Meet Mira.
lines: Meet Mira, an intelligent travel booking assistant built for Ceylon Compass Holidays,
combining conversational intelligence with reliable business logic.

title: How Mira works
lines: Mira separates conversational understanding from critical business operations.
Its agent workflow supports Gemini, while pricing, interface validation and publishing permissions are enforced through deterministic code.

title: Quick Booking
lines: We start with a traveller asking for a Sigiriya day trip.
This booking uses local rules for intent extraction.
For two adults, the workbook returns 315 dollars. The full amount is due as a deposit.
Mira saves the quote and a private enquiry.
The simulated payment declines. A retry confirms the booking.

title: Custom Journey Planning
lines: This ten-day family request also uses local rules.
Mira builds the itinerary from published destinations. The first stop is Ella.
Selecting Kandy on the map changes the day and photograph together.
These recommended tours visit the places the family asked about.
A specialist receives the bespoke enquiry. Mira gives no custom price.
The traveller switches to the Cultural Triangle package for two adults on May third.
The total is 2,125 dollars, with a 532-dollar deposit.

title: Engineering evidence
lines: The backend quoted May third. The workspace kept January tenth and disabled checkout.
I synchronized the quote and traveller state, preserving stale-quote protection, and restored the itinerary components.
Checkout is enabled for the correct party. Seven targeted regression tests passed.

title: Grounding and Safety
lines: Mira cites the published payment policy, P zero one. It gives the deposit and balance terms.
This departure is outside the rate window. A specialist receives the enquiry, with no estimated price.
Asked for internal costs and margin, Mira offers a standard quote and keeps the figures private.

title: Staff Enquiry Management
lines: Staff open the enquiry created in the first booking.
The private view shows a buy cost of 66,000 rupees, gross margin and quote history.
The enquiry links to the trace of the original request.
Staff mark the traveller as contacted and save an internal follow-up note.

title: Human-Governed Content
lines: Staff ask Mira to prepare a private Hill Country journey using published Ella material.
The audit records Gemini generating this draft. The staff role can review the text, but cannot publish it.
Role-based authorization lets the approver publish the reviewed draft.
The new source is now available for retrieval and appears in the traveller catalogue.

title: Tracing and Evaluation
lines: This is the original Sigiriya trace. Intent extraction used local rules.
The trace follows retrieval, workbook pricing, validated interface components and persistence.
The saved report shows 53 of 54 cases passed. That’s 98.1 percent.
The judge scored ten of ten review cases. Human calibration is pending.

title: Mira.
lines: Mira brings together intelligent conversations, reliable pricing and accountable AI.
Thank you for watching.
